newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Nine hurt as police, slum-dwellers clash in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Nine hurt as police, slum-dwellers clash in Brazil.

text.p: Nine people were injured and 40 arrested when about 400 police clashed with people living in a shanty-town on the outskirts of Brasilia on Friday, an official said.

The fighting broke out when police and government officials arrived at the Estrutural slum to remove illegal businesses operating in the area, said a spokesman for the Federal District, which includes the Brazilian capital.
A government official and a police officer were in hospital after being shot during the violence but their injuries were not serious, the spokesman said.
"The resistance was planned," he said. "The police were attacked with petrol bombs and stones."
National Globo television showed images of police officers firing tear gas canisters at a crowd of slum-dwellers hurling rocks and sticks.

The riot was the second in less than a month in the shanty-town. Eleven people were injured in fighting in July when police and officials demolished about 400 shacks built illegally in an environmental reserve.
